result.title: RouterWorld: Scaling Conversational AI with Latency-Aware LLM Routing
result.summary: Conversational AI systems built on Large Language Models (LLMs) require routing mechanisms that balance answer quality and response latency at scale. However, existing LLM routing benchmarks assume full observability of all candidate model outcomes, under-emphasize latency as a first-class metric, and fragment evaluation across heterogeneous protocols misaligned with real-world settings. We introduce RouterWorld, a comprehensive benchmark for LLM routing in conversational GenAI. RouterWorld unifies 371k single-turn responses and 76k multi-turn agentic trajectories, adopts natural user interactions with a standardized LLM-as-a-judge protocol, and decouples efficiency from transient pricing via hardware-grounded latency annotations. Crucially, RouterWorld formalizes routing under partial observability through two setups: Cold-Start, which restricts learning to sparse, static logs, and Voyager, which models continuous data streams where routing decisions shape future training distributions. Evaluating 13 routing baselines, we find that most routers over-emphasize accuracy while ignoring latency under partial observability. Code and benchmark data are publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RouterWorld 基准，统一 37.1 万条单轮回答与 7.6 万多轮 agentic 轨迹，在 Cold-Start 与 Voyager 两种部分可观测设定下评测 13 种 LLM 路由基线，并指出多数路由器偏重准确率而忽视延迟。
AI.relevance_reason: 路由中的延迟-质量权衡与「何时继续思考、何时停止」的计算分配结构相似，其部分可观测及「决策改变未来数据流」的在线设定，可能为 LVR 的停止决策与成本评价提供类比线索，可供核查。
